guide: Open Start and type your organization name, your cost-to-raise-one-dollar setting, the value of a volunteer hour and the number of days for names, payments and benefits.
Replace the demo data: clear the demo rows and type your own events in Events, then your tickets, sponsors, auction items, event gifts, costs and hours in their sheets.
Keep Events up to date: date, venue, budget cost, goal and expected guests. Actual cost, raised money and the go or no-go verdict fill in by themselves.
Record every ticket in Event Tickets and every sponsor in Sponsors with the amount promised, the amount received and the benefits owed and delivered.
Record auction and raffle items with a fair value and a starting bid, and write the sold price and the buyer when the item sells.
Enter every event cost in Event Costs and every gift in Event Gifts. Event Result then shows net raised, cost per dollar and net per guest against last year.
Before booking, use the Event Go or No-go and the Break-even Solver with low, expected and high guests; they show the net and the cost line to cut.
Open Campaigns for the goal and dates, then Campaign Progress and Campaign by Week to see the thermometer, the pace needed and the forecast to finish.
Use the Sponsor Renewal List and the Benefit Tracker every month to see who to call and which benefits are due.
Use the 18 calculators for your decisions, print 12 sheets and 12 documents, follow 12 checklists and tap a message link to send a text with the details already written in.
Read the Events and Campaigns Dashboard and the charts every month. A founder who runs one event a year can start with the Event Go or No-go and the First Small Event checklist.

This is a standard workbook with no macros: it works offline, you own the file, and it keeps all your figures in one place that you can read, check and change. It is not an accounting system or a tax record.

listing.title: Nonprofit Events and Campaigns Excel Template: Event Budget, Tickets, Sponsors, Auction, Campaign Goal and Forecast
listing.headline: Know what each event really raised and what each campaign will finish at
listing.description:
Run the event and campaign side of fundraising in one Excel workbook. Built for a development manager, an executive director and a founder with volunteers who hold one or more events a year and run appeals and campaigns around them. Events holds each event with date, venue, budget cost, goal and expected guests. Event Tickets lists every ticket by type with the benefit value of each ticket set apart, so the gift part of a ticket is shown on its own. Sponsors lists each sponsor with the level, the money promised and received, the benefits owed and delivered and the next step. Auction Items records fair value, starting bid, sold price and buyer. Event Gifts, Event Costs and Event Hours add the gifts on the night, the direct costs and the staff and volunteer hours.

Event Result works out raised, costs, net, cost to raise one dollar and net per guest and compares them with your own last year. The Sponsor Renewal List ranks who to call, and the Benefit Tracker shows what is due. Campaigns, Campaign Progress and Campaign by Week show the goal, the thermometer, pledges apart from cash, days left, the pace needed and a forecast to finish. Campaign Comparison and Method Ranking set three years side by side and rank each way of raising money by what it costs.

18 calculators include an event result card, a go or no-go test with low, expected and high sales, a break-even solver, a cost line watcher, a sponsor package pricer, a campaign thermometer, a finish forecast and a cheapest method ranker. Print 12 sheets and 12 documents, follow 12 checklists and send 34 ready text messages to guests, table hosts, sponsors, auction donors, donors, the venue, the caterer and your team.

This is part four of the Nonprofit Organization suite. A standard .xlsx workbook with no macros and no subscription, with a demo copy full of sample data to explore first. Donors and guests appear by name, contact status, amounts and dates only. It helps you keep track of your own figures and does not promise results. Check your local rules for gift receipts and benefits, and ask your adviser about tax.
